newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU raps France, Italy and Greece on social laws.
newsitem.headline: EU raps France, Italy and Greece on social laws.

text.p: The European Commission has rapped France, Italy and Greece for failing to introduce certain European Union laws related to social affairs and warned it will take them to court unless they act within two months.

In a statement, social affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said so-called "reasoned opinions" had been sent to the three countries -- the last stage of a complaints procedure before the matter goes to the European Court of Justice.
Italy was rapped for forcing foreign university lecturers to accept temporary contracts while their Italian colleagues obtained permanent employment.

Although Italy did change its laws to outlaw this in 1995, the Commission said the fact that lecturers already in service had to sign new contracts -- sometimes with revised terms of service and job descriptions -- was discriminatory.
France is accused of failing to respect the principle of equal treatment in social security regarding agreements between the EU and Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Turkey.
The Commission said France had refused to pay certain benefits such as handicap allowances to eligible nationals from those countries.
The Commission's complaint against Greece centres on differences in pensions paid to men and women working for the National Institute of Social Security.
